+# Hosted billing
+
+`internal/hosted/billing` holds the credit and payment rules for the hosted
+service: a credit gate, an append-only credit ledger, a weekly margin check, an
+open-source programme, and Stripe webhook and client contracts. The code and
+its tests exist, but it is not deployed. See
+[Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md) for the wider service.
+
+The package is logic plus interfaces. Every database, Stripe API and publishing
+operation is an interface (`LedgerStore`, `BalanceReader`, `SkipPublisher`,
+`MarginStore`, `MarginAlerter`, `OSSStore`, `StripeEventStore`, `StripeClient`,
+`PortalClient`). The repository contains no non-test implementation of any of
+them; the tests use in-memory stubs. The only non-test code outside the package
+that imports it is `internal/hosted/publicsite/pricing.go`, which reads
+`DefaultMinimumMargin`.
+
+The package defines no prices, plans or credit amounts. Credits are plain
+`int64` counts supplied by callers.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `gate.go` | Decide whether a review may run on the available credits, and publish an explanation when it may not. |
+| `ledger.go` | Validate and build grant, reserve, settle and refund transactions. |
+| `margin.go` | Compute weekly gross margin per installation and alert when it is low. |
+| `oss.go` | Accept and decide open-source programme applications. |
+| `stripe.go` | Verify Stripe webhooks and validate arguments to Stripe client calls. |
+
+## Credit gate
+
+`CreditGate.Authorize(ctx, installationID, required)` reads the balance through
+`BalanceReader.Balance` and returns a `ReviewDecision`.
+
+| Case | `Allowed` | `SkipCode` | Error returned |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Nil reader, `installationID <= 0` or `required <= 0` | false | empty | yes |
+| Balance read fails | false | `billing_unavailable` | yes, wrapped as `read credit balance` |
+| `available < required` | false | `credits_exhausted` | no |
+| `available >= required` | true | empty | no |
+
+The gate fails closed: if the balance cannot be read, the review is not
+allowed. Every decision that passes argument validation carries a `Summary`
+written for the pull request reader. The skip summaries state that no AI
+review ran.
+
+`Authorize` only reads the balance. It does not write a reservation, although
+the allowed summary says credits were "reserved". Reserving is a separate call
+on `Ledger`; the package has no function that performs both.
+
+`CreditEnforcer.Enforce(ctx, installationID, reviewID, required)` wraps the
+gate. It requires a non-nil `SkipPublisher` and a non-empty `reviewID`. When the
+decision is allowed it returns without publishing. Otherwise it calls
+`SkipPublisher.PublishSkippedReview` with the decision, including when the gate
+returned an error. If both the gate and the publisher fail, the two errors are
+combined with `errors.Join`; otherwise the gate error is returned in preference
+to the publish error.
+
+## Credit ledger
+
+A `Transaction` has an `InstallationID`, an optional `ReviewID`, an
+`IdempotencyKey`, a `Kind` and a signed `Credits` value that is the change to
+the available balance.
+
+| `Ledger` method | Kind | `Credits` written | Required arguments |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `Grant` | `grant` | `+credits` | store, positive installation, `credits > 0`, key |
+| `Reserve` | `reserve` | `-credits` | the above plus a non-empty `reviewID` |
+| `Settle` | `settle` | `reserved - actualCredits` | a valid reservation, `actualCredits >= 0`, key |
+| `Refund` | `refund` | `+reserved` | a valid reservation, key |
+
+A valid reservation (`validReservation`) has a positive installation, a
+non-empty `ReviewID`, kind `reserve` and negative `Credits`.
+
+`Settle` returns the unused part of a reservation. In the test, reserving 6 and
+settling at 4 returns 2. `Settle` does not cap `actualCredits` at the reserved
+amount, so a higher actual cost produces a negative settle entry. `Refund`
+returns the whole reservation.
+
+`Grant`, `Settle` and `Refund` call `LedgerStore.Append`. `Reserve` calls
+`LedgerStore.Reserve`, whose contract is to append the negative entry only when
+the installation has at least the required credits, and to serialize that
+check. Both store methods return the transaction and a boolean; the test stub
+returns the earlier transaction and `false` when the idempotency key was
+already used. The `Ledger` methods add no idempotency logic of their own beyond
+requiring a key.
+
+### `credit_transactions` table
+
+Migration `0011_credit_ledger` defines the table the ledger is designed for.
+
+| Rule | Definition |
+| --- | --- |
+| Idempotency | `UNIQUE (installation_id, idempotency_key)`; key length 1 to 200 |
+| Review ID | Text, default empty, at most 200 characters |
+| Kinds | `grant`, `reserve`, `settle`, `refund` |
+| Sign | `reserve` must be negative; `grant` and `refund` must be positive; `settle` may be any value |
+| One reservation per review | Unique index on `(installation_id, review_id)` where kind is `reserve` |
+| One terminal entry per review | Unique index on `(installation_id, review_id)` where kind is `settle` or `refund` |
+| Append-only | Trigger `credit_transactions_append_only` raises on any `UPDATE` or `DELETE` |
+| Tenant isolation | Row level security is enabled and forced; policy `tenant_isolation` compares `installation_id` with the `px1.installation_id` setting |
+
+Rows are deleted only through `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `installations`.
+
+## Margin guardrail
+
+`EvaluateMargin(e, minimum)` computes
+`(RevenueMicros - LLMCostMicros) / RevenueMicros` for one `WeeklyEconomics`
+row.
+
+- It returns an error for a non-positive installation, a zero `WeekStart`, or
+  negative revenue or cost.
+- With zero revenue it returns `Available: false`, no alert, and a reason
+  saying margin is unavailable.
+- A `minimum` that is `<= 0` or `>= 1` is replaced by `DefaultMinimumMargin`,
+  which is `0.60`.
+- `Alert` is true when the margin is strictly below the minimum. The margin can
+  be negative when cost exceeds revenue.
+
+`MarginJob.Run(ctx, week)` requires a `MarginStore` and a `MarginAlerter`. It
+normalizes `week` to Monday 00:00 UTC (`utcWeek`), loads rows with
+`MarginStore.WeeklyEconomics`, and for each row:
+
+1. Fails if the row's `WeekStart` is not the requested week.
+2. Evaluates the margin with `MarginJob.Minimum`.
+3. Calls `MarginStore.RecordMargin`, which reports whether the record was newly
+   created.
+4. Calls `MarginAlerter.AlertLowMargin` only when the record was newly created
+   and the result is an alert.
+
+It returns the number of alerts sent. Alert deduplication therefore depends on
+the store: a re-run for a week already recorded sends nothing. The job stops at
+the first error and returns the alerts sent so far.
+
+Migration `0014_margin_guardrails` defines `weekly_billing_metrics`, keyed by
+`(installation_id, week_start)`, with non-negative `revenue_micros` and
+`llm_cost_micros`, a nullable `margin`, `low_margin`, `recorded_at` and
+`alerted_at`. A check requires `margin` to be null exactly when revenue is
+zero. Row level security is enabled and forced with the same `tenant_isolation`
+policy.
+
+`internal/hosted/publicsite/pricing.go` uses `DefaultMinimumMargin` in
+`MaxStandardReviewCostMicrousd` to derive a cost ceiling from plan revenue.
+
+## Open-source programme
+
+`OSSProgramme` has a `Store` and an `ApprovalCredits` amount. The package sets
+no default for `ApprovalCredits`.
+
+`Apply` validates an `OSSApplication` and submits it with status `submitted`.
+It requires a positive installation and repository ID, a non-empty
+`ContactEmail`, a `Reason` that is not blank, and a repository URL that passes
+`publicHTTPSRepository`. That function checks only the URL's form: scheme
+`https`, a non-empty host, no user info and no fragment. It does not contact
+the host, does not check that the repository is public, and does not require a
+particular host. The email is checked only for being non-empty.
+
+`Decide(ctx, installationID, applicationID, actor, approve, reason)` requires
+all of those values, with a non-blank reason. A rejection records status
+`rejected` with no credits. An approval requires `ApprovalCredits > 0` and
+records status `approved` with `CreditGrant` set to that amount. It calls
+`OSSStore.Decide` with `submitted` as the expected current status; the store
+contract is to record the decision and any credit grant atomically. The test
+stub refuses a second decision on the same application.
+
+Migration `0013_oss_programme` defines `oss_applications`. The repository URL
+must start with `https://`, the contact email is 3 to 320 characters, the
+reason is 1 to 4000 characters, and `credit_grant` is non-negative. A check
+ties status to the decision fields: `submitted` rows have no `decided_at` or
+`decided_by`, and decided rows have both. A composite foreign key to
+`repositories(installation_id, id)` ties each application to a repository in
+the same installation. Row level security is enabled and forced.
+
+## Stripe webhook
+
+`StripeWebhook.Handle(ctx, body, signature)` verifies a webhook and dispatches
+it. The checks run in this order, and each failure returns an error before any
+store call.
+
+1. `Secret` is non-empty and `Store` is non-nil.
+2. The body is non-empty and at most `MaxStripeEventBytes` (`1 << 20`, 1 MiB).
+3. `parseStripeSignature` reads the comma-separated header. It needs a `t`
+   value that parses as a non-zero integer and at least one `v1` value. Parts
+   without `=` and other keys are ignored.
+4. The timestamp is within `Tolerance` of the current time in either direction.
+   A `Tolerance` of zero or less means 5 minutes. `Now` replaces `time.Now`
+   when set.
+5. The expected signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<body>` with
+   `Secret`. Each `v1` value is hex-decoded and compared with `hmac.Equal`,
+   which is constant-time. One match is enough; values that are not valid hex
+   are skipped.
+6. The body decodes as JSON with a non-empty `id` and a non-empty
+   `data.object`.
+
+| Event type | Store call |
+| --- | --- |
+| `invoice.paid` | `StripeEventStore.InvoicePaid(ctx, eventID, object)` |
+| `customer.subscription.updated` | `StripeEventStore.SubscriptionUpdated(ctx, eventID, object)` |
+| Any other type | None; `Handle` returns nil |
+
+The handler passes the raw `data.object` JSON through without interpreting it.
+It does not map the event to an installation, grant credits or record the event
+itself. Replay protection in this package is the timestamp window only;
+deduplication by event ID is left to the store.
+
+Migration `0012_stripe_billing` defines the tables for that store.
+`stripe_events` has `event_id` as its primary key (1 to 200 characters), an
+`installation_id`, and an `event_type` limited to the two types above.
+`stripe_accounts` has one row per installation with a unique `customer_id`
+matching `^cus_[A-Za-z0-9]+$`, plus `subscription_id`, `subscription_status`
+(default `inactive`) and `price_id`. Both tables have row level security
+enabled and forced.
+
+## Stripe client helpers
+
+Three functions validate arguments and then call a `StripeClient` or
+`PortalClient`. Each returns an error without calling the client when
+validation fails.
+
+| Function | Validation | Client call |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `ProvisionCustomer` | Positive installation; billing email contains `@` | `EnsureCustomer` |
+| `RecordMeteredReview` | Customer ID starts with `cus_`; price ID starts with `price_`; non-empty event ID; `credits > 0`; non-zero time | `ReportMeteredUsage`, with the time converted to UTC |
+| `OpenCustomerPortal` | Customer ID starts with `cus_`; return URL starts with `https://` | `CreatePortalSession` |
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- No store, Stripe API client, skip publisher or margin alerter exists outside
+  the tests.
+- No HTTP handler, worker or scheduler calls this package.
+- Nothing connects the gate, the ledger and metered usage reporting into one
+  review flow.
+- `invoice.paid` and `customer.subscription.updated` payloads are not parsed,
+  and no code turns a paid invoice into a credit grant.
+- No price IDs, plan definitions or credit grant amounts are defined here.

+title: Cascading configuration
+section: concepts
+kind: narrative
+status: shipped
+covers:

+verified_at:
+---
+
+# Cascading configuration
+
+`config_cascade.go` resolves the px1 settings that apply to one file. It reads
+a `.px1/config.json` at the repository root and one in each directory on the
+way down to the file, validates each, and merges them into a single result.
+
+Status: shipped, through one command. `px1 validate-config` (in
+`validate_config.go`, dispatched from `main.go`) calls
+`resolveCascadingConfig` and prints the result as JSON; see the
+[CLI reference](CLI_REFERENCE.md). That is the only caller. No review command
+in the repository reads the resolved values, so today the cascade can be
+checked and inspected but does not change what a review does.
+
+## Which files are read
+
+`configCandidates(target)` lists the candidate paths, root first. For the
+target `src/api/handler.go` it returns:
+
+```
+.px1/config.json
+src/.px1/config.json
+src/api/.px1/config.json
+```
+
+A target in the repository root has one candidate, `.px1/config.json`.
+Missing files are skipped. Files beside the cascade path (for example
+`docs/.px1/config.json` for a target under `src/`) are never read.
+
+## Target rules
+
+`resolveCascadingConfig(target, files)` takes a repository-relative path and a
+map from candidate path to file content. It rejects the target with
+`config target must be a repository-relative file` when the target is empty,
+is absolute, cleans to `.` or `..`, or starts with `../` after cleaning.
+
+The target's directory may be at most `configDepthLimit` (20) levels deep.
+Deeper targets fail with `config target exceeds directory depth limit`. The
+target file itself does not have to exist.
+
+## Fields
+
+`decodeConfig` validates one file. The same rules are published as
+`docs/config.schema.json`.
+
+| Field | Type | Rule |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `version` | integer | Required; must be `1` |

+

+| --- | --- |
+| `strictness` | 2 |
+| `commentTypes` | `logic`, `security`, `style`, `syntax` |
+| `maxInlineComments` | 15 |
+| `failOnP0` | false |
+| `disabledRules` | none |
+| `contextRepos` | none |

+
+Files are applied in candidate order: repository root first, then each
+directory down to the one containing the target. A field that a file omits
+leaves the current value unchanged. How a present field merges depends on the
+field:

+| --- | --- | --- |

+| `failOnP0` | Logical OR | Once any file sets `true`, a deeper `false` does not turn it off |
+| `maxInlineComments` | Last file wins | The deepest file that sets it decides |
+| `commentTypes` | Last file wins, whole list replaced | Lists are not combined |
+| `disabledRules` | Union across all files | Sorted; a deeper file cannot re-enable a rule |
+| `context.repos` | Union across all files, lower-cased | Sorted; duplicates that differ only in case collapse |
+
+The function's comment states the principle for the two gating settings:
+they only become stricter.
+
+The union of `context.repos` is checked again after merging. If the resolved
+list has more than 10 repositories the call fails with
+`resolved context.repos cannot exceed 10 repositories`, even when every file
+is within its own limit of 10.
+
+Every file that was found and applied is recorded, in order, in `sources`.
+
+## Worked example
+
+From `TestResolveCascadingConfigKeepsGatesStrict`, resolving
+`src/api/handler.go` with three files:
+
+| File | Content |
+| --- | --- |
+| `.px1/config.json` | `{"version":1,"strictness":3,"failOnP0":true,"maxInlineComments":10,"disabledRules":["root-rule"]}` |
+| `src/.px1/config.json` | `{"version":1,"strictness":1,"failOnP0":false,"maxInlineComments":20,"commentTypes":["logic"],"disabledRules":["child-rule"]}` |
+| `src/api/.px1/config.json` | `{"version":1,"maxInlineComments":5}` |
+
+Result:
+
+| Setting | Value | Why |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `strictness` | 3 | Root sets 3; the `src` value of 1 is lower and ignored |
+| `failOnP0` | true | Root sets `true`; the `src` value of `false` does not undo it |
+| `maxInlineComments` | 5 | Deepest file wins over 10 and 20 |
+| `commentTypes` | `logic` | `src` replaces the default list; `src/api` does not set it |
+| `disabledRules` | `child-rule`, `root-rule` | Union of both lists, sorted |
+| `sources` | all three paths | Root first |
+

+`Acme/API` in the root file and `acme/api`, `acme/web` in `src`. The resolved
+`contextRepos` is `acme/api`, `acme/web`.
+
+## Output
+
+`resolvedConfig` is what `px1 validate-config` prints, as one line of JSON
+with the keys `sources`, `strictness`, `commentTypes`, `disabledRules`,
+`maxInlineComments`, `failOnP0` and `contextRepos`. `contextRepos` is omitted
+when empty. Note the output key is `contextRepos`, while the input field is
+`context.repos`.
+
+## Errors
+
+Any invalid file stops resolution. The error is prefixed with the path of the
+file that failed, for example `src/.px1/config.json: version must be 1`.
+There is no partial result and no fallback to defaults.
+
+| Message | Cause |
+| --- | --- |
+| `config must be non-empty and at most 64 KiB` | Empty or oversized file |
+| `config contains trailing data` | More than one JSON value |
+| `version must be 1` | Missing or different `version` |
+| `strictness must be between 1 and 3` | Out of range |
+| `maxInlineComments must be between 1 and 50` | Out of range |
+| `commentTypes contains an invalid or duplicate value` | Unknown or repeated type |
+| `disabledRules contains an invalid id` | Blank or longer than 80 bytes |
+| `disabledRules contains a duplicate id` | Repeated within one file |
+| `context.repos cannot exceed 10 repositories` | More than 10 in one file |
+| `context.repos contains an invalid or duplicate owner/repository` | Bad shape or repeated entry |
+
+Unknown fields and malformed JSON return the JSON decoder's own error.
+
+## How `px1 validate-config` uses it
+
+`runValidateConfig` takes `--root` (default `.`) and `--path` (default
+`README.md`) and accepts no positional arguments.
+
+1. It calls `resolveCascadingConfig` with an empty file map. This validates
+   the target before any file is read, so an absolute path or one that
+   escapes the root is rejected first.
+2. It reads each candidate from disk under `--root`. A file that does not
+   exist is skipped; any other read error fails as `read PATH: ...`.
+3. It resolves again with the files it found and prints the JSON.
+
+The files are read from the working tree at `--root`, not from a git commit.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- No command other than `validate-config` reads the resolved configuration.
+- No environment variable, flag or organisation-level layer; the cascade is
+  only the `.px1/config.json` files on the path to the target.
+- No way for a deeper directory to lower `strictness`, clear `failOnP0`,
+  re-enable a disabled rule or remove a context repository.
+- The schema file is not loaded by the code; the Go checks are separate and
+  slightly stricter (they also reject whitespace-only rule ids and `.` or `..`
+  as a repository owner or name).

+---
+title: GitHub App delivery
+section: concepts
+kind: narrative
+status: built

+---
+
+# GitHub App delivery
+
+`internal/hosted/githubapp` holds the code that talks to GitHub as an
+installed GitHub App: it mints installation tokens, sends rate-limit-aware API
+requests, publishes check runs, reviews and a sticky summary comment, parses
+`@px1` comment commands, and polls reactions. The package is built: the code
+and tests exist, but it is not deployed. No non-test Go code outside the
+package imports it, so nothing in the hosted service calls it yet.
+
+See [Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md) for the surrounding service,
+[GitHub App registration](GITHUB_APP_REGISTRATION.md) for the App itself, and
+[SCM providers](SCM_PROVIDERS.md) for the provider-neutral interface.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | Main identifiers | Purpose |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `client.go` | `AppMinter`, `CachedTokenSource`, `Client` | Authentication and the HTTP client |
+| `checks.go` | `CheckRunPublisher`, `ReviewConclusion` | Check run start and completion |
+| `review.go` | `ReviewPublisher`, `MaxInlineReviewComments` | One pull request review with inline comments |
+| `summary.go` | `StickySummaryPublisher`, `StaticReviewCommentMarker` | Create or update one summary comment |
+| `commands.go` | `ParseCommand`, `CommandAuthorizer` | `@px1` commands and the permission check |
+| `remember.go` | `RememberHandler`, `ExplicitMemory` | Store a memory from `@px1 remember` |
+| `forget.go` | `ForgetHandler` | Delete a memory from `@px1 forget` |
+| `reactions.go` | `ReactionPoller` | Collect thumbs up and thumbs down on review comments |
+
+Every publisher takes a `BaseURL`, which defaults to `https://api.github.com`
+when empty, and a client with one method,
+`Do(ctx, installationID, request)`. That method is declared three times, as
+`APIClient`, `CheckAPIClient` and `SummaryAPIClient`; `Client` satisfies all
+three.
+
+## Authentication
+
+### `AppMinter`
+
+`AppMinter.Mint` exchanges a GitHub App JWT for an installation token.
+
+1. It requires a non-empty `AppID`, a non-nil RSA `PrivateKey`, and an
+   installation ID greater than zero. The code comment says the key is
+   supplied by the deployment secrets manager; the package does not load it.
+2. `signAppJWT` builds an RS256 token with `iss` set to the App ID, `iat` set
+   30 seconds in the past, and `exp` 9 minutes in the future.
+3. It sends `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` with no body, so the
+   request does not narrow the token to particular repositories or
+   permissions.
+4. A status outside 200 to 299 returns an error with the status code only.
+5. The response is decoded through a 1 MiB limit into a `Token` with `Value`
+   and `ExpiresAt`.
+
+When `HTTP` is nil it uses `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout.
+
+### `CachedTokenSource`
+
+`CachedTokenSource` wraps a `Minter` and keeps tokens in a map in process
+memory. Nothing writes them to disk or a database.
+
+- A cached token is reused while the current time plus `Skew` is before its
+  expiry. `Skew` defaults to 2 minutes when zero or negative.
+- Concurrent calls for the same installation share one mint. Waiting callers
+  receive the same token or error, or their own context error if it ends
+  first.
+- A minted token that is empty, or that already expires within the skew, is
+  turned into an error and not cached.
+- Failed mints are not cached; the next call tries again.
+
+## The `Client`
+
+`Client.Do` sends one request as an installation and handles retries.
+
+It reads the whole request body into memory so it can be replayed, with no
+size limit. On every attempt it fetches a token from `Tokens` and sets three
+headers on a clone of the request, overwriting any existing values:
+
+| Header | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Authorization` | `Bearer ` followed by the installation token |
+| `Accept` | `application/vnd.github+json` |
+| `X-GitHub-Api-Version` | `2022-11-28` |
+
+### Retry rules
+
+A request is retryable only if its method is `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS`, or
+it carries an `X-GitHub-Idempotency-Key` header. Other requests are sent
+exactly once. None of the publishers in this package set that header, so
+their `POST` and `PATCH` calls are never replayed.
+
+`MaxRetries` defaults to 3 when zero or negative, giving at most four attempts.
+
+For a retryable request, `retryDelay` decides whether a response should be
+retried and how long to wait. Only status 429, 403, and 500 or above are
+considered:
+
+| Condition, checked in order | Wait |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Retry-After` is a number of seconds | That many seconds |
+| `Retry-After` is an HTTP date | Until that time |
+| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` is `0` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` parses | Until the reset time |
+| Status is 429, or 500 or above | `backoff(attempt)` |
+| Otherwise (a 403 with none of the above) | Not retried |
+
+`backoff` is 1 second doubled per attempt, capped at 32 seconds. Waits taken
+from `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-Reset` have no upper bound in the client;
+only the context can cut them short. Negative waits become zero.
+
+A transport error on a retryable request is retried with `backoff`. When
+retries run out, or the request is not retryable, `Do` returns the last
+response with a nil error. Callers must check the status code themselves, and
+every publisher here does.
+
+## Check runs
+
+`CheckRunPublisher` creates and completes a check run named `px1 review`.
+
+`Start` posts to `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs` with status
+`in_progress`, the run ID as `external_id`, the details URL, and the output
+title `px1 review in progress`. It returns the check run ID, and fails if
+GitHub returns an ID that is not positive.
+
+`Complete` patches the check run to `completed` with a conclusion, a
+`completed_at` time in UTC, a title and summary, and one action button:
+label `Retry review`, identifier `RetryReviewAction` (`retry_review`).
+
+| Input | Rule |
+| --- | --- |
+| Owner and repository | Letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` only; not `.` or `..` |
+| `HeadSHA` | Exactly 40 hexadecimal characters |
+| `RunID` | Non-empty after trimming |
+| `DetailsURL` | Parses with scheme `http` or `https` and a host |
+| `Conclusion` | Only `neutral` or `failure` |
+| `Title` (on completion) | Non-empty after trimming |
+| Summary text | Cut at 60,000 bytes, then `[truncated by px1]` is appended |
+
+The summary cut is by byte offset, so it can split a multi-byte character.
+
+`ReviewConclusion(hasP0, failOnP0)` returns `failure` only when both are
+true, and `neutral` otherwise. The package never reports `success`.
+
+Nothing in this package handles the `retry_review` action when a user clicks
+it.
+
+## Pull request reviews
+
+`ReviewPublisher.Create` posts all inline findings in one request to
+`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews`.
+
+- The review `event` is always `COMMENT`. The package never approves or
+  requests changes.
+- `commit_id` is the validated 40-character head SHA.
+- The body is prefixed with `<!-- px1-review-run:{RunID} -->`.
+- More than `MaxInlineReviewComments` (15) findings is an error; nothing is
+  sent and nothing is dropped silently.
+- Each finding must pass `review.Finding.Validate`.
+
+`RunID` must be 1 to 100 characters from letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`.
+This stops a run ID from closing the HTML comment early; a test rejects
+`run --> forged` before any request is made.
+
+Each comment is placed on the `RIGHT` side at the finding's `EndLine`. When
+`StartLine` differs, `start_line` and `start_side` are sent as well. The
+comment body shows severity, title, body, evidence and confidence to two
+decimals. A suggestion is wrapped in a `suggestion` code fence, and the fence
+is lengthened until it does not appear inside the suggestion text.
+
+The code comment states that `Create` does not retry and that the caller's
+durable run state is the idempotency boundary.
+
+## Sticky summary
+
+`StickySummaryPublisher.Upsert` keeps one summary comment per pull request.
+
+The body must start with `StaticReviewCommentMarker`
+(`<!-- px1-static-review -->`). `find` then pages through the issue comments,
+100 per page, looking for a comment where all three hold:
+
+- `user.type` is `Bot`,
+- `user.login` equals the `botLogin` argument, ignoring case,
+- the body contains the marker.
+
+If one is found it is updated with `PATCH`, and `Upsert` returns `updated`.
+Otherwise a new comment is created with `POST`, and it returns `created`. A
+comment by a normal user that contains the marker is ignored, which a test
+covers.
+
+`MaxPages` defaults to 10. If the last allowed page is full, `find` returns
+`PR comment search reached its page limit` and nothing is posted. Each page is
+decoded through a 2 MiB limit.
+
+## Comment commands
+
+`ParseCommand` reads only the first non-empty line of a comment. The line must
+start with `@px1` (any case) followed by a command word (any case).
+
+| Command | Arguments | Result |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `@px1 review` | none | `Name: review` |
+| `@px1 ignore` | none | `Name: ignore` |
+| `@px1 why` | none | `Name: why` |
+| `@px1 explain PATH` | exactly one path | `Path` cleaned to forward slashes |
+| `@px1 remember TEXT` | one or more words | `Text`, words joined by single spaces, at most 2000 bytes |
+| `@px1 forget ID` | exactly one ID | `MemoryID` lowercased |
+
+Extra arguments make `review`, `ignore`, `why`, `explain` and `forget`
+invalid. The `explain` path must be relative and must not be `.`, `..`, or
+start with `../` after cleaning. The `forget` ID must be 36 characters of
+hexadecimal with hyphens at positions 8, 13, 18 and 23.
+
+`ParseCommand` only parses. The package has handlers for `remember` and
+`forget`; it has none for `review`, `ignore`, `why` or `explain`.
+
+### Permission check
+

# GitHub App delivery
`internal/hosted/githubapp` holds the code that talks to GitHub as an
installed GitHub App: it mints installation tokens, sends rate-limit-aware API
requests, publishes check runs, reviews and a sticky summary comment, parses
`@px1` comment commands, and polls reactions. The package is built: the code
and tests exist, but it is not deployed. No non-test Go code outside the
package imports it, so nothing in the hosted service calls it yet.
See [Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md) for the surrounding service,
[GitHub App registration](GITHUB_APP_REGISTRATION.md) for the App itself, and
[SCM providers](SCM_PROVIDERS.md) for the provider-neutral interface.
## Files
| File | Main identifiers | Purpose |
| `client.go` | `AppMinter`, `CachedTokenSource`, `Client` | Authentication and the HTTP client |
| `checks.go` | `CheckRunPublisher`, `ReviewConclusion` | Check run start and completion |
| `review.go` | `ReviewPublisher`, `MaxInlineReviewComments` | One pull request review with inline comments |
| `summary.go` | `StickySummaryPublisher`, `StaticReviewCommentMarker` | Create or update one summary comment |
| `commands.go` | `ParseCommand`, `CommandAuthorizer` | `@px1` commands and the permission check |
| `remember.go` | `RememberHandler`, `ExplicitMemory` | Store a memory from `@px1 remember` |
| `forget.go` | `ForgetHandler` | Delete a memory from `@px1 forget` |
| `reactions.go` | `ReactionPoller` | Collect thumbs up and thumbs down on review comments |
Every publisher takes a `BaseURL`, which defaults to `https://api.github.com`
when empty, and a client with one method,
`Do(ctx, installationID, request)`. That method is declared three times, as
`APIClient`, `CheckAPIClient` and `SummaryAPIClient`; `Client` satisfies all
three.
## Authentication
### `AppMinter`
`AppMinter.Mint` exchanges a GitHub App JWT for an installation token.
1. It requires a non-empty `AppID`, a non-nil RSA `PrivateKey`, and an
installation ID greater than zero. The code comment says the key is
supplied by the deployment secrets manager; the package does not load it.
2. `signAppJWT` builds an RS256 token with `iss` set to the App ID, `iat` set
30 seconds in the past, and `exp` 9 minutes in the future.
3. It sends `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` with no body, so the
request does not narrow the token to particular repositories or
permissions.
4. A status outside 200 to 299 returns an error with the status code only.
5. The response is decoded through a 1 MiB limit into a `Token` with `Value`
and `ExpiresAt`.
When `HTTP` is nil it uses `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout.
### `CachedTokenSource`
`CachedTokenSource` wraps a `Minter` and keeps tokens in a map in process
memory. Nothing writes them to disk or a database.
- A cached token is reused while the current time plus `Skew` is before its
expiry. `Skew` defaults to 2 minutes when zero or negative.
- Concurrent calls for the same installation share one mint. Waiting callers
receive the same token or error, or their own context error if it ends
first.
- A minted token that is empty, or that already expires within the skew, is
turned into an error and not cached.
- Failed mints are not cached; the next call tries again.
## The `Client`
`Client.Do` sends one request as an installation and handles retries.
It reads the whole request body into memory so it can be replayed, with no
size limit. On every attempt it fetches a token from `Tokens` and sets three
headers on a clone of the request, overwriting any existing values:
| Header | Value |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer ` followed by the installation token |
| `Accept` | `application/vnd.github+json` |
| `X-GitHub-Api-Version` | `2022-11-28` |
### Retry rules
A request is retryable only if its method is `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS`, or
it carries an `X-GitHub-Idempotency-Key` header. Other requests are sent
exactly once. None of the publishers in this package set that header, so
their `POST` and `PATCH` calls are never replayed.
`MaxRetries` defaults to 3 when zero or negative, giving at most four attempts.
For a retryable request, `retryDelay` decides whether a response should be
retried and how long to wait. Only status 429, 403, and 500 or above are
considered:
| Condition, checked in order | Wait |
| `Retry-After` is a number of seconds | That many seconds |
| `Retry-After` is an HTTP date | Until that time |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` is `0` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` parses | Until the reset time |
| Status is 429, or 500 or above | `backoff(attempt)` |
| Otherwise (a 403 with none of the above) | Not retried |
`backoff` is 1 second doubled per attempt, capped at 32 seconds. Waits taken
from `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-Reset` have no upper bound in the client;
only the context can cut them short. Negative waits become zero.
A transport error on a retryable request is retried with `backoff`. When
retries run out, or the request is not retryable, `Do` returns the last
response with a nil error. Callers must check the status code themselves, and
every publisher here does.

`CheckRunPublisher` creates and completes a check run named `px1 review`.
`Start` posts to `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/check-runs` with status
`in_progress`, the run ID as `external_id`, the details URL, and the output

GitHub returns an ID that is not positive.

`completed_at` time in UTC, a title and summary, and one action button:
label `Retry review`, identifier `RetryReviewAction` (`retry_review`).
| Input | Rule |
| Owner and repository | Letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.` only; not `.` or `..` |
| `HeadSHA` | Exactly 40 hexadecimal characters |
| `RunID` | Non-empty after trimming |
| `DetailsURL` | Parses with scheme `http` or `https` and a host |
| `Conclusion` | Only `neutral` or `failure` |
| `Title` (on completion) | Non-empty after trimming |
| Summary text | Cut at 60,000 bytes, then `[truncated by px1]` is appended |
The summary cut is by byte offset, so it can split a multi-byte character.
`ReviewConclusion(hasP0, failOnP0)` returns `failure` only when both are
true, and `neutral` otherwise. The package never reports `success`.

it.

`ReviewPublisher.Create` posts all inline findings in one request to

durable run state is the idempotency boundary.

`StickySummaryPublisher.Upsert` keeps one summary comment per pull request.

+# Hosted report publishing and access
+
+The `internal/hosted/report` package does two jobs for the hosted service. It
+publishes a static review bundle for one commit to object storage
+(`publish.go`), and it provides the pieces needed to decide whether a signed-in
+GitHub user may read a repository's report (`access.go`).
+
+Status: built. The code and its tests exist, but the hosted service is not
+deployed (see [Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md)). No other package
+in the repository imports this one, and it contains no HTTP handler and no
+object store implementation.
+
+## Publishing a bundle
+
+### Types
+
+| Identifier | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `ExportRequest` | `Root` (repository checkout), `BaseSHA`, `HeadSHA` |
+| `Exporter` | Interface with `Export(ctx, request, outputDir)`; writes the bundle into a directory |
+| `CLIExporter` | `Exporter` that runs the px1 binary |
+| `Object` | One upload: `Key`, `ContentType`, `SHA256`, `Body`, `Size`, `Immutable` |
+| `ObjectStore` | Interface with `Put(ctx, object)` |
+| `Publisher` | Holds an `Exporter`, an `ObjectStore` and `MaxBundleBytes` |
+
+### Flow of `Publisher.Publish`
+
+`Publish(ctx, owner, repo, request)` returns the list of object keys it
+uploaded.
+
+1. Validate the inputs (see below). On failure it returns
+   `exporter, store, repository, root, and full SHAs are required`.
+2. Create a temporary directory named `px1-report-*`. It is removed when the
+   function returns.
+3. Call `Exporter.Export` to write the bundle into that directory.
+4. For each of the three required files, in order: check it, add its size to
+   the running total, read it and compute its SHA-256.
+5. Upload the three objects with `ObjectStore.Put`, in the same order.
+
+All three files are read and checked before the first upload starts. If a
+`Put` fails, the error is returned as `upload FILE: ...`; objects already
+uploaded in that call are not removed.
+
+### Bundle contents
+
+| File | Content type |
+| --- | --- |
+| `index.html` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` |
+| `review.json` | `application/json` |
+| `checksums.sha256` | `text/plain; charset=utf-8` |
+
+Each file is checked with `os.Lstat` and must be a regular file. A missing
+file, a directory or a symbolic link fails with
+`report output FILE is missing or not regular`. The test
+`TestPublisherRequiresCompleteBundle` covers an export that writes only
+`index.html`.
+
+### Object keys and metadata
+
+Each key has the form:
+
+```
+reports/OWNER/REPO/HEADSHA/FILE
+```
+
+`HeadSHA` is used as given; it is not lower-cased. Every object is created
+with `Immutable: true`, `SHA256` set to the lower-case hex digest of the body,
+and `Size` set to the body length. How a store enforces `Immutable` is up to
+the `ObjectStore` implementation; none exists in the repository.
+
+### Input validation and limits
+
+| Check | Rule |
+| --- | --- |
+| `owner`, `repo` | `validObjectSlug`: non-empty, not `.` or `..`, only ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.` |
+| `BaseSHA`, `HeadSHA` | `fullSHA`: exactly 40 hexadecimal characters, either case |
+| `Root` | Non-empty |
+| `Exporter`, `Store` | Non-nil |
+| Bundle size | Sum of the three file sizes must not exceed the limit |
+
+The size limit is `Publisher.MaxBundleBytes` when it is greater than zero.
+Otherwise it is `maxBundleBytes`, 50 MiB (`50 << 20` bytes). Exceeding it
+returns `report bundle exceeds N bytes`. Because the slug rule excludes `/`
+and the SHA rule excludes everything but hex digits, no caller-supplied value
+can add a path segment to an object key.
+
+### `CLIExporter`
+
+`CLIExporter.Export` runs:
+
+```
+BINARY export-review --root ROOT --base BASESHA --head HEADSHA --out OUTPUTDIR
+```
+
+`BINARY` is the `Binary` field, or the running executable (`os.Executable`)
+when the field is empty. The type's comment states the intent: it invokes the
+trusted px1 executable, not repository code. Standard output and standard
+error are discarded. A failure is wrapped as `export static report: ...`.
+The `export-review` command is described in the
+[CLI reference](CLI_REFERENCE.md).
+
+## Report access
+
+`access.go` contains a GitHub OAuth web flow (`OAuthFlow`) and a repository
+read check (`AccessAuthorizer`).
+
+### `OAuthFlow`
+
+Fields: `ClientID`, `ClientSecret`, `CallbackURL`, `StateKey`, `HTTP`,
+`AuthorizeURL`, `TokenURL` and `Now` (a clock override used by tests).
+
+`Begin(redirect, sessionBinding)` returns the URL to send the browser to. It
+fails unless:
+
+- `ClientID` is non-empty;
+- `CallbackURL` parses with scheme `http` or `https` and a host;
+- `StateKey` is at least 32 bytes;
+- `redirect` passes `safeRedirect`: starts with `/`, does not start with `//`,
+  and contains no carriage return or line feed;
+- `sessionBinding` is at least 16 bytes.
+
+The state payload is JSON with four fields: `redirect`, `expires` (10 minutes
+from now, Unix seconds), `nonce` (16 random bytes from `crypto/rand`,
+base64url) and `binding` (base64url SHA-256 of `sessionBinding`). The state
+string is the base64url payload, a dot, and the base64url HMAC-SHA256 of the
+payload under `StateKey`.
+
+The authorize URL is `AuthorizeURL`, or
+`https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize` when empty, with query parameters
+`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope` set to `read:user repo`, and `state`.
+
+`ValidateState(state, sessionBinding)` returns the stored redirect path. It
+returns `invalid OAuth state` when:
+
+- the state is not exactly two dot-separated parts;
+- either part is not valid base64url;
+- the HMAC does not match (compared with `hmac.Equal`);
+- the payload is not valid JSON, the nonce is empty, or the redirect fails
+  `safeRedirect`;
+- the binding does not equal the hash of the supplied `sessionBinding`.
+
+It returns `expired OAuth state` when the current time is later than
+`expires`. `ValidateState` does not re-check the length of `StateKey`; only
+`Begin` does. The package keeps no record of used nonces.
+
+The test `TestOAuthStateIsSignedScopedAndExpires` shows a tampered state, a
+state presented with a different session binding, and a state checked 11
+minutes later all being rejected.
+
+`Exchange(ctx, code)` trades the code for a GitHub access token. It requires
+`ClientID`, `ClientSecret` and a non-blank code. It sends a JSON `POST` with
+`client_id`, `client_secret`, `code` and `redirect_uri` to `TokenURL`, or
+`https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` when empty. The response must
+have status 200 and a non-empty `access_token`; the body is read through a
+1 MiB limit. Any other outcome returns
+`GitHub OAuth exchange failed: status N`. The token is returned to the caller;
+this package does not store it.
+
+### `AccessAuthorizer`
+
+`CanRead(ctx, oauthToken, owner, repo)` asks GitHub whether the user's token
+can see the repository. It requires a non-empty token and an owner and repo
+that pass `slug` (the same character rule as `validObjectSlug`). It sends
+`GET BASE/repos/OWNER/REPO` with `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` and
+`Accept: application/vnd.github+json`. `BASE` is `BaseURL`, or
+`https://api.github.com` when empty.
+
+| GitHub status | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| 200 | `true`, no error |
+| 403 or 404 | `false`, no error |
+| Anything else | `false` and `check GitHub repository access: status N` |
+
+Nothing is cached: each call makes one GitHub request.
+
+### HTTP clients
+
+`Exchange` and `CanRead` use the `HTTP` field when set and
+`http.DefaultClient` otherwise. The default client has no timeout, so a
+deadline must come from the context or from a supplied client.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- No HTTP routes: nothing here serves a report, sets a session cookie or
+  handles the OAuth callback.
+- No `ObjectStore` implementation, and no code that reads a published bundle
+  back.
+- No storage or refresh of the GitHub access token.
+- No link between `Publish` and `CanRead`; a caller must combine them.
+- No deletion or expiry of published objects.

error are discarded. A failure is wrapped as `export static report: ...`.

| 403 or 404 | `false`, no error |
| Anything else | `false` and `check GitHub repository access: status N` |

`Exchange` and `CanRead` use the `HTTP` field when set and
`http.DefaultClient` otherwise. The default client has no timeout, so a
deadline must come from the context or from a supplied client.

handles the OAuth callback.

back.
- No storage or refresh of the GitHub access token.
- No link between `Publish` and `CanRead`; a caller must combine them.
- No deletion or expiry of published objects.

+# Issue tracker and Slack integrations
+
+Two packages under `internal/hosted/integrations` connect the hosted service
+to outside tools. `issues` reads one Linear or Jira issue with a tenant's
+OAuth token. `slack` verifies Slack requests, completes the Slack OAuth
+install, builds a review message and parses the `/px1 status` command.

+## Issue trackers (`issues`)
+
+### Types
+
+| Identifier | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Provider` | `Linear` (`"linear"`) or `Jira` (`"jira"`) |
+| `Issue` | `Provider`, `Key`, `Title`, `Description`, `AcceptanceCriteria`, `URL` |
+| `Tracker` | Interface with `FetchIssue(ctx, installationID, key)`; both clients satisfy it |
+| `TokenSource` | Interface with `OAuthToken(ctx, installationID, provider)`; returns the bearer token for one tenant |
+| `OAuthGrant` | `Provider`, `AccountID`, `BaseURL`, `AccessToken`, `RefreshToken`, `ExpiresAt` |
+| `OAuthExchanger` | Interface with `ExchangeOAuthCode(ctx, provider, code, redirectURI)` |
+| `ConnectionStore` | Interface with `SaveOAuthConnection(ctx, installationID, grant)` |
+
+The only caller in the repository is the agentic review toolbox: the
+`read_issue` tool holds an `issues.Tracker` in `Toolbox.Issues` and fetches
+only keys listed in the review scope. See [Agentic review tools](AGENT_TOOLS.md).
+
+### Connecting a tracker
+
+`CompleteOAuth` finishes an OAuth connection. The caller passes the
+installation ID and provider; the function's comment says these must come from
+the already-verified dashboard session, not from callback query parameters.
+
+It rejects the call before any network request unless all of these hold:
+
+- the exchanger and store are non-nil;
+- `installationID` is greater than zero;
+- `provider` is `Linear` or `Jira`;
+- `code` is non-empty;
+- `redirectURI` starts with `https://`.
+
+It then calls `ExchangeOAuthCode`. The grant is rejected if its `Provider`
+differs from the requested one, or if `AccountID` or `AccessToken` is empty.
+A valid grant is passed to `SaveOAuthConnection`. Token refresh is not
+implemented in this package; `RefreshToken` and `ExpiresAt` are only carried.
+

+
+`DetectIssueKeys(branch, pullBody)` upper-cases both strings and collects
+matches of `issueKeyPattern`:
+
+```
+\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[1-9][0-9]*\b
+```
+
+That is a project prefix of 2 to 10 characters starting with a letter, a
+hyphen, and a number with no leading zero. The branch is scanned first, then
+the body. Duplicates are dropped, collection stops at 10 keys, and the result
+is sorted. In the test, branch `feature/eng-123` and body
+`Implements OPS-9 and ENG-123` give `ENG-123`, `OPS-9`.
+
+### Extracting acceptance criteria
+
+`ExtractAcceptanceCriteria(description)` reads the description line by line:
+
+- A line that equals `acceptance criteria` or `acceptance criterion`, after
+  trimming `#`, `*`, `:` and spaces and lower-casing, starts the section.
+- Inside the section, a line starting with `#` ends the scan.
+- Checkbox lines (`- [ ] `, `- [x] `, `- [X] `) are collected wherever they
+  appear before the scan ends, including before the section heading.
+- Plain bullets (`- ` or `* `) are collected only inside the section.
+- The scan stops at 20 criteria.
+

+
+Both clients have the fields `HTTP`, `Tokens` and `BaseURL`.
+
+| Client | Request | Checks |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `LinearClient` | `POST` of a GraphQL query `issue(id: $id)` asking for `identifier`, `title`, `description`, `url`. +that contains a valid key.

+are kept, arrays are walked, and for an object it follows `text` if present,
+otherwise `content`. Non-blank strings are joined with newlines. The Jira
+issue URL is built as `BaseURL` + `/browse/KEY`. The Jira client does not check
+that the returned key is non-empty.
+
+Both clients run `ExtractAcceptanceCriteria` on the description and return the
+result in `Issue.AcceptanceCriteria`.

+
+The unexported `request` function sends every call:
+
+- It fails with `OAuth token source and tenant are required` if `Tokens` is
+  nil or the installation ID is not positive.
+- It asks `TokenSource.OAuthToken` for the token. An error or an empty token
+  becomes `OAuth token is unavailable`; the underlying error is not returned.
+- It sets `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` and `Accept: application/json`, plus
+  `Content-Type: application/json` when there is a body.
+- If `HTTP` is nil it uses a client with a 10 second timeout.
+- A status outside 200 to 299 returns `PROVIDER returned status N`. The body
+  is drained, not returned.
+- The response is read through a limit of `maxIssueResponse`, 2 MiB
+  (`2 << 20` bytes).
+

+
+### Verifying a Slack request
+
+`VerifyRequest(secret, timestamp, signature, body, now)` checks the signature
+Slack puts on each request. It returns `Slack request signature is invalid`
+when the secret is empty, the body is larger than `MaxSlackBodyBytes`
+(1 MiB, `1 << 20` bytes), or the signature does not start with `v0=`.
+
+The timestamp must parse as a Unix second count and be within 5 minutes of
+`now` in either direction; otherwise the error is
+`Slack request timestamp is outside tolerance`.
+
+The expected value is HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:TIMESTAMP:BODY` with the signing
+secret. The supplied signature is hex-decoded and compared with `hmac.Equal`,
+a constant-time comparison. The tests cover a changed body and a request
+replayed 10 minutes later; both are rejected.
+
+### OAuth state
+
+`OAuthState` carries `InstallationID`, `Nonce` and `ExpiresAt` (Unix seconds).
+
+`SignOAuthState` requires a positive installation ID, a non-empty nonce, a
+positive expiry and a non-empty secret. The output is the base64url JSON
+payload, a dot, and the base64url HMAC-SHA256 of that encoded payload. The
+caller chooses the expiry; the package sets no maximum lifetime.

+before decoding the payload, then rejects the state if the JSON is invalid,
+the installation ID is not positive, the nonce is empty, or `now` is later
+than `ExpiresAt`.
+

+
+`CompleteOAuth(ctx, client, store, code, signedState, stateSecret, now)`:
+
+1. Requires a non-nil `OAuthClient`, a non-nil `InstallationStore` and a
+   non-empty code.
+2. Verifies the signed state. The tenant comes from the state, not from the
+   request.
+3. Calls `OAuthClient.ExchangeOAuthV2(ctx, code)`.
+4. Rejects a grant with an empty `TeamID` or `BotToken`.
+5. Rejects a grant whose `Scopes` lack `chat:write` or `commands`.
+6. Calls `SaveSlackInstallation` with the state's installation ID, the grant
+   and the state's nonce.
+
+The package does not track used nonces. It passes the nonce to the store; what
+the store does with it is not shown in this code.
+
+### Review message
+
+`ReviewMessage(repository, pull, p0, summary, reviewURL)` returns a `Message`
+with fallback `Text` and three `Blocks`: a `header` block with the heading as
+`plain_text`, a `section` with the summary as `mrkdwn`, and a `section` with a
+link to `reviewURL` labelled `Open commit-pinned review`.
+
+| Input | Rule |
+| --- | --- |
+| `repository` | Non-empty, at most 200 bytes |
+| `pull` | Greater than zero |
+| `p0` | Zero or more |
+| `summary` | Non-empty, at most 2800 bytes |
+| `reviewURL` | Starts with `https://` |
+
+The heading is `px1 review: REPO !N`. When `p0` is greater than zero it
+becomes an alert emoji followed by `N P0 finding(s): REPO !N`. The function
+does not escape the summary or the URL.
+
+### Status command
+
+`ParseStatusCommand(body)` parses a form-encoded slash command body into a
+`StatusCommand` (`ResponseURL`, `Repository`, `PullNumber`).
+
+- The body must be non-empty and at most `MaxSlackBodyBytes`.
+- `command` must be exactly `/px1`.
+- `text` must be exactly three fields: `status`, a repository containing `/`,
+  and a positive pull request number with an optional leading `#`.
+- `response_url` must start with `https://hooks.slack.com/`.
+
+Usage errors return `usage: /px1 status owner/repo PR`. This function does not
+verify the signature; the caller must run `VerifyRequest` first.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- No HTTP routes or handlers for OAuth callbacks, Slack commands or events.
+- No implementation of `TokenSource`, `OAuthExchanger`, `ConnectionStore`,
+  `OAuthClient` or `InstallationStore`.
+- No code that sends a `Message` to Slack or replies to a `ResponseURL`.
+- No token refresh, and no write access to Linear or Jira.
+- `slack` is not imported by any other package in the repository.

+
+# Feedback learning
+
+`internal/hosted/learning` turns reviewer feedback into bounded signals:
+classified replies, stored memories, noise suppression, rule proposals and
+weekly metrics. The code and its tests exist, but it is not deployed. See
+[Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md) for the wider service.
+
+The package comment states the principle: model classifications are evidence,
+not authority over a pull request.
+
+The package is logic plus interfaces. Storage, clustering, the model call and
+GitHub publishing are all interfaces (`ReplyStore`, `ReplyModel`,
+`ThreadReplier`, `MemoryStore`, `MemoryCatalogStore`, `RuleInferenceStore`,
+`CommentClusterer`, `RuleProposalPublisher`, `ProposalQueueStore`,
+`ProposalPullRequestPublisher`). The repository contains no non-test
+implementation of any of them, and no non-test code outside the package
+imports it.
+
+Every entry point that takes a tenant rejects an `installationID` or
+`repositoryID` that is zero or negative.
+
+## Files
+
+| File | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `replies.go` | Classify a reviewer's reply to a finding and answer questions. |
+| `memory.go` | Retrieve memories for a review prompt, with a hard cap. |
+| `catalog.go` | Page through memories for display, requiring evidence. |
+| `suppression.go` | Decide whether a finding is hidden because similar ones were ignored. |
+| `inference.go` | Propose repository rules from recurring human review comments. |
+| `proposal_queue.go` | Edit, reject or accept a queued rule proposal. |
+| `metrics.go` | Aggregate one week of review outcomes for a repository. |
+
+## Reply classification
+
+`ReplyProcessor.Process(ctx, input)` classifies one reply with one model call.
+
+Validation, before the model is called:
+
+- `Model` and `Store` are set; `Provider` and `ModelName` are not blank.
+- `InstallationID`, `RepositoryID`, `CommentID` and `ActorID` are positive and

+| --- | --- |
+| Strict JSON | Unknown fields are rejected; any data after the first JSON value is rejected |

+the kind is `question`, the answer is posted with
+`ThreadReplier.ReplyToComment`. A `question` with a nil `Replier` returns an
+error, but only after the classification has been saved. A model, decode,
+store or reply failure returns an error and an empty classification.
+
+`Confidence` is validated and stored but no code in the package acts on it. No
+migration defines a table for reply classifications.
+
+## Memory retrieval
+
+A `Memory` has an `ID`, `Scope`, `Kind`, `Text`, optional `PathGlob` and
+`Language`, a `Weight`, `EvidenceLinks` and `LastConfirmedAt`.
+
+`RetrieveMemories(ctx, store, query)` fetches memories for a prompt.
+
+- It requires a store, a positive tenant, a `Path`, a `Language` and a
+  non-empty `Embedding`.
+- The path is cleaned and converted to forward slashes. Absolute paths, `..`
+  and paths starting with `../` are rejected.
+- `Limit` is forced to `MaxPromptMemories` (20) when it is zero, negative or

+Migration `0007_memories` defines the table.
+
+| Column or rule | Definition |
+| --- | --- |
+| `scope` | `organization`, `repository`, `path` or `language` |

+and category `logic` return `Suppress: false` whatever the feedback history

+recorded.

+
+`ProposalQueue` manages a `QueuedRuleProposal`, whose `State` is `pending`,
+`publishing`, `accepted` or `rejected`.
+
+Every operation first loads the proposal (`loadProposal`) and rejects it unless
+the returned ID, installation and repository equal the ones requested, the rule
+text is not blank, and there is at least one evidence link. Each link must be
+an `https` URL on `github.com` with a non-empty path. Checking the returned
+tenant against the request means a store that returns another tenant's row
+causes an error.

+| `Reject` | `pending` | Calls `RejectPendingProposal` |
+| `Accept` | `pending` or `publishing` | Opens a pull request and returns its URL |

+   return an error ("proposal is no longer pending"). From `publishing`, skip
+   the claim, which lets an interrupted accept be retried.
+2. Call `ProposalPullRequestPublisher.OpenProposal`, which the interface
+   requires to be idempotent for the proposal ID.

+which opens pull requests directly.

+
+`AggregateWeeklyMetrics(installationID, repositoryID, week, outcomes)` builds

+inclusive and the end exclusive. Outcomes outside the week are skipped.

+| --- | --- |

+| `DownvoteRate` | Sum of `Downvoted` divided by `Comments`; 0 with no comments |
+| `Suppressed` | Sum of `Suppressed` |
+
+The call fails if any outcome has an empty `PullRequestID`, a negative count,
+or `Addressed` or `Downvoted` greater than `Comments`. A `PullRequestID` that
+repeats one already counted in the week also fails.
+
+The function computes only; it does not store. Migration
+`0008_weekly_repository_metrics` defines `weekly_repository_metrics`, keyed by
+`(installation_id, repository_id, week_start)`, with a check that `week_start`
+is a Monday, both rates between 0 and 1, and row level security enabled and
+forced.
+
+## Not implemented
+
+- No store, clusterer, model adapter or GitHub publisher exists outside the
+  tests.
+- No worker, scheduler or HTTP handler calls this package.
+- No code writes memories, or turns a classified reply or a suppression
+  decision into a memory.
+- `DecideSuppression` returns a decision; nothing here applies it to a review.
+- No migration exists for reply classifications, rule proposal fingerprints or
+  the proposal queue.

+
+# Onboarding demo reviews
+
+The `internal/hosted/onboarding` package queues one demo review per repository
+for a new installation. For each repository it looks up the latest merged pull
+request and enqueues a review of that pull request's head commit, labelled as
+a demo.
+
+Status: built. The code and its tests exist, but the hosted service is not
+deployed (see [Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md)). The package is
+one file, `demo.go`. No other package in the repository imports it, and the
+two interfaces it depends on have no implementation outside its tests.
+
+## Types
+
+| Identifier | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Repository` | `InstallationID`, `RepositoryID`, `Owner`, `Name` |
+| `MergedPull` | `Number`, `HeadSHA`, `URL`, `MergedAt` |
+| `DemoReview` | The queued job: `InstallationID`, `RepositoryID`, `PullNumber`, `HeadSHA`, `SourceURL`, `IdempotencyKey`, `Provenance` |
+| `MergedPullReader` | Interface with `LatestMergedPull(ctx, repository)`; returns the pull request, a found flag and an error |
+| `DemoReviewQueue` | Interface with `EnqueueDemoReview(ctx, job)`; returns whether a new job was created |
+| `DemoScheduler` | Holds `Pulls` (a `MergedPullReader`) and `Queue` (a `DemoReviewQueue`) |
+
+## Flow of `DemoScheduler.Schedule`
+
+`Schedule(ctx, installationID, repositories)` returns the number of jobs newly
+created.
+
+1. Validate the call. `Pulls` and `Queue` must be non-nil, `installationID`
+   must be greater than zero, and the list must hold between 1 and
+   `MaxDemoRepositories` (20) repositories. Otherwise it returns
+   `pull reader, queue, tenant, and one to twenty repositories are required`.
+2. For each repository, in order:
+   - Check that it belongs to the installation and is well formed (see
+     below).
+   - Call `LatestMergedPull`. If nothing is found, skip the repository.
+   - Validate the returned pull request.
+   - Build a `DemoReview` and call `EnqueueDemoReview`.
+   - Count the job only if the queue reports it was created.
+
+## Validation
+
+| Subject | Rule | Error |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Repository | `InstallationID` equals the `installationID` argument, `RepositoryID` is positive, `Owner` and `Name` are non-empty, and the `RepositoryID` has not appeared earlier in the list | `demo repositories must be unique and belong to the installation` |
+| Pull request | `Number` is positive, `HeadSHA` passes `fullSHA`, `MergedAt` is not the zero time, and `URL` starts with `https://` | `latest merged pull request is invalid` |
+
+`fullSHA` requires exactly 40 hexadecimal characters in either case.
+
+The repository check is the tenant boundary: a repository whose
+`InstallationID` differs from the caller's is rejected before any pull request
+lookup for it. `TestDemoSchedulerRejectsCrossTenantRepository` covers this.
+
+## The queued job
+
+| Field | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| `InstallationID` | The `installationID` argument |
+| `RepositoryID` | From the repository |
+| `PullNumber` | `MergedPull.Number` |
+| `HeadSHA` | `MergedPull.HeadSHA`, lower-cased |
+| `SourceURL` | `MergedPull.URL` |
+| `IdempotencyKey` | `demo:INSTALLATION:REPOSITORY:HEADSHA`, with the lower-cased SHA |
+| `Provenance` | A fixed sentence, below |
+
+The provenance text is always:
+
+```
+Demo review of the latest merged pull request selected during installation. It does not represent the current default branch or a live pull request.
+```
+
+## Idempotency
+
+The scheduler does not remember what it has queued. Deduplication is the
+queue's job: `EnqueueDemoReview` returns `false` when it did not create a job,
+and the scheduler then leaves the count unchanged. In the test, the queue
+stub keys on `IdempotencyKey`; a second `Schedule` call with the same
+repository returns a count of 0.
+
+Because the key includes the head SHA, a repository whose latest merged pull
+request has changed produces a different key.
+
+## Error handling
+
+`Schedule` stops at the first error and returns it together with the count so
+far. Errors from `LatestMergedPull` and `EnqueueDemoReview` are returned
+unchanged. Jobs enqueued before the error stay enqueued; there is no rollback.

# Onboarding demo reviews
The `internal/hosted/onboarding` package queues one demo review per repository
for a new installation. For each repository it looks up the latest merged pull
request and enqueues a review of that pull request's head commit, labelled as
a demo.
Status: built. The code and its tests exist, but the hosted service is not
deployed (see [Hosted architecture](HOSTED_ARCHITECTURE.md)). The package is
one file, `demo.go`. No other package in the repository imports it, and the
two interfaces it depends on have no implementation outside its tests.
## Types
| Identifier | Purpose |
| `Repository` | `InstallationID`, `RepositoryID`, `Owner`, `Name` |
| `MergedPull` | `Number`, `HeadSHA`, `URL`, `MergedAt` |
| `DemoReview` | The queued job: `InstallationID`, `RepositoryID`, `PullNumber`, `HeadSHA`, `SourceURL`, `IdempotencyKey`, `Provenance` |
| `MergedPullReader` | Interface with `LatestMergedPull(ctx, repository)`; returns the pull request, a found flag and an error |
| `DemoReviewQueue` | Interface with `EnqueueDemoReview(ctx, job)`; returns whether a new job was created |
| `DemoScheduler` | Holds `Pulls` (a `MergedPullReader`) and `Queue` (a `DemoReviewQueue`) |
## Flow of `DemoScheduler.Schedule`
`Schedule(ctx, installationID, repositories)` returns the number of jobs newly
created.
1. Validate the call. `Pulls` and `Queue` must be non-nil, `installationID`
must be greater than zero, and the list must hold between 1 and
`MaxDemoRepositories` (20) repositories. Otherwise it returns
`pull reader, queue, tenant, and one to twenty repositories are required`.
2. For each repository, in order:
- Check that it belongs to the installation and is well formed (see
below).
- Call `LatestMergedPull`. If nothing is found, skip the repository.
- Validate the returned pull request.
- Build a `DemoReview` and call `EnqueueDemoReview`.
- Count the job only if the queue reports it was created.
## Validation
| Subject | Rule | Error |

| Repository | `InstallationID` equals the `installationID` argument, `RepositoryID` is positive, `Owner` and `Name` are non-empty, and the `RepositoryID` has not appeared earlier in the list | `demo repositories must be unique and belong to the installation` |
| Pull request | `Number` is positive, `HeadSHA` passes `fullSHA`, `MergedAt` is not the zero time, and `URL` starts with `https://` | `latest merged pull request is invalid` |
`fullSHA` requires exactly 40 hexadecimal characters in either case.
The repository check is the tenant boundary: a repository whose
`InstallationID` differs from the caller's is rejected before any pull request
lookup for it. `TestDemoSchedulerRejectsCrossTenantRepository` covers this.
## The queued job
| Field | Value |
| `InstallationID` | The `installationID` argument |
| `RepositoryID` | From the repository |
| `PullNumber` | `MergedPull.Number` |
| `HeadSHA` | `MergedPull.HeadSHA`, lower-cased |
| `SourceURL` | `MergedPull.URL` |
| `IdempotencyKey` | `demo:INSTALLATION:REPOSITORY:HEADSHA`, with the lower-cased SHA |
| `Provenance` | A fixed sentence, below |
The provenance text is always:
Demo review of the latest merged pull request selected during installation. It does not represent the current default branch or a live pull request.
## Idempotency
The scheduler does not remember what it has queued. Deduplication is the
queue's job: `EnqueueDemoReview` returns `false` when it did not create a job,
and the scheduler then leaves the count unchanged. In the test, the queue
stub keys on `IdempotencyKey`; a second `Schedule` call with the same
repository returns a count of 0.
Because the key includes the head SHA, a repository whose latest merged pull
request has changed produces a different key.
## Error handling
`Schedule` stops at the first error and returns it together with the count so
far. Errors from `LatestMergedPull` and `EnqueueDemoReview` are returned
unchanged. Jobs enqueued before the error stay enqueued; there is no rollback.

adds nothing to the count.

not show how the latest merged pull request is chosen or how the job is run.
